name: Harvard CS50P
description: Learn Python through ten units of lectures, problem sets, and a final project.
bestFor: A structured first Python course with hands-on assignments.
free: Open course materials and a CS50 course certificate after meeting the requirements.
limitation: The optional verified edX certificate is a separate paid credential.

name: Python for Everybody
description: Learn Python for working with files, web data, and databases.
bestFor: Beginners interested in practical data tasks.
free: The course site offers lessons, a textbook, and assignments.
limitation: Sign in for the gradebook and autograded assignments. External course platforms have separate terms.

name: Python Programming MOOC
description: Work through the University of Helsinki introductory and advanced Python courses.
bestFor: Learners who prefer lots of coding exercises.
free: Public course material for both courses.
limitation: The 2026 edition closes at year-end. Passing requires exercises and an exam.

name: The Python Tutorial
description: Use the official introduction to Python syntax, modules, and core data structures.
bestFor: Programmers picking up Python as a new language.
free: Public documentation and self-contained examples.
limitation: The tutorial assumes some prior programming experience.

name: Automate the Boring Stuff with Python
description: Read Al Sweigart’s practical Python book and automate everyday computer tasks.
bestFor: Beginners who want projects involving files and spreadsheets.
free: The book is free to read on the author’s site.
limitation: Printed copies and some companion products are separate.

name: Exercism Python Track
description: Practice Python with a progression of exercises and automated feedback.
bestFor: Building fluency after learning basic Python syntax.
free: The Python track includes free exercises, feedback, and mentoring.
limitation: Sign up to join the track and track progress.

name: MIT OpenCourseWare
description: Explore materials from MIT courses at your own pace.
bestFor: Self-study with university-level lecture notes and assignments.
free: Published MIT course materials are freely available without registration.
limitation: Materials vary by course. MIT OpenCourseWare provides no degree, credit, or certificate.

name: OpenLearn
description: Take self-paced introductory courses from The Open University.
bestFor: Exploring a new subject with a short course before committing to formal study.
free: OpenLearn courses are free to study, and selected courses offer digital badges.
limitation: Register for participation records and badges. Availability varies by course.

name: GitHub Pages
description: Publish a static portfolio or project site directly from a GitHub repository.
bestFor: A personal portfolio, documentation site, or demo.
free: GitHub Free includes Pages from public repositories. You can create a free personal account and verify your email without setting up billing.
limitation: GitHub restricts online businesses, e-commerce, and commercial SaaS on Pages.

name: Cloudflare Pages
description: Deploy a static site from a Git repository or upload your build directly.
bestFor: A static portfolio or project site that you update from Git.
free: The Free plan includes static deployments with up to 500 builds per month.
limitation: The documented Pages build and file limits still apply. Functions have separate Workers quotas.

name: Carrd
description: Build a responsive one-page portfolio, profile, or landing page without code.
bestFor: Publishing a simple site quickly from a template.
free: Create up to three basic sites per free account.
limitation: Custom domains and forms require a Pro plan.

name: Codeberg Pages
description: Publish a static site from a repository on the Codeberg nonprofit forge.
bestFor: Open source project pages, developer blogs, and web experiments.
free: Codeberg Pages hosts static sites for free.
limitation: Set up a Codeberg repository. Static-site generation or deployment automation takes additional configuration.

name: GitLab Pages
description: Publish static project sites using GitLab CI/CD.
bestFor: A portfolio or docs site for code already hosted on GitLab.
free: Pages is included in GitLab’s Free tier.
limitation: Requires a GitLab CI/CD pipeline. Dynamic server-side processing is outside the Pages model.

name: Neocities
description: Build a hand-coded personal website in your browser and publish it on a Neocities subdomain.
bestFor: Learning HTML or making a small personal site.
free: A free static site with a browser-based HTML editor.
limitation: Custom domains and higher limits come with a paid Supporter plan.

name: Vercel
description: Deploy personal frontend projects with Vercel’s Hobby plan.
bestFor: A personal portfolio or non-commercial frontend application.
free: The Hobby tier includes deployments with monthly usage allowances.
limitation: Hobby is for personal, non-commercial use. Usage limits reset on the plan’s schedule.

name: PDF24
description: Compress, merge, split, and convert PDFs with a browser tool for each task.
bestFor: One-off PDF edits, conversions, and smaller files.
free: Use the browser tools for free without an account. A separate free Creator app is available for Windows.
limitation: Many browser tools upload files for processing. Use the desktop Creator for local processing on Windows.

name: PDFsam Basic
description: Merge, split, rotate, and extract PDF pages locally on your computer.
bestFor: Rearranging or combining sensitive documents offline.
free: The free desktop app handles page operations without watermarks.
limitation: Basic focuses on page operations. Visual editing is a separate product.

name: NAPS2
description: Scan paper documents, reorder pages, and create searchable PDFs.
bestFor: Turning physical paperwork into searchable digital files.
free: Free scanning and OCR software for Windows, macOS, and Linux.
limitation: Scanning requires a compatible device and drivers. OCR quality depends on the scan.

name: OCRmyPDF
description: Add a searchable text layer to a scanned PDF with a local command-line tool.
bestFor: Batch processing scanned files and making text selectable.
free: The project provides a free Python application and library.
limitation: Installation requires command-line tools and dependencies. OCR can misread poor scans.

name: PDFtk Free
description: Merge or split PDF pages in a simple Windows desktop interface.
bestFor: Light PDF page management without uploading files.
free: The free edition includes the graphical tool and PDFtk Server command-line utility.
limitation: PDFtk Free is for Windows and advanced features are in the Pro edition.

name: LibreOffice
description: Write documents, edit spreadsheets, and export office files to PDF on your computer.
bestFor: Offline office work and file conversion without a subscription.
free: Writer, Calc, Impress, Draw, and other office tools are free.
limitation: Complex Microsoft Office layouts may need a check after conversion.

name: Stirling PDF
description: Run a private PDF toolkit for merging, conversion, and document processing.
bestFor: People comfortable self-hosting a PDF tool for private files.
free: The self-hosted server starts on a Free plan.
limitation: Self-hosting requires setup. Team and Enterprise features have separate licenses.

name: Openverse
description: Search openly licensed and public-domain images and audio from many collections.
bestFor: Finding reusable media across multiple archives in one search.
free: The search engine is free to use, with license and source filters.
limitation: Check the original item page before reuse. Attribution and adaptation terms vary by file.

name: Wikimedia Commons
description: Find freely licensed and public-domain photos, illustrations, and audiovisual files.
bestFor: Sourcing historical images, maps, and educational media.
free: Public file pages and downloads provide access to the media and licensing details.
limitation: Each file has its own terms. Some require credit, notice, or sharing adaptations under the same license.

name: The Met
description: Find open-access images of public-domain artworks in The Met collection.
bestFor: Art, history, and design projects that need reusable museum images.
free: Download art marked Open Access under the CC0 dedication.
limitation: Use the Open Access filter or badge. Other collection images have different terms.

name: Art Institute of Chicago
description: Browse a museum collection with downloadable images of public-domain works.
bestFor: Reusing historical artwork and design references.
free: Marked public-domain artworks are available for free reuse.
limitation: Open the artwork’s details and verify its rights designation. Other items can remain protected.

name: Smithsonian Open Access
description: Explore and download Smithsonian open-access images, data, and 3D models.
bestFor: Projects that need original museum materials or 3D assets.
free: Items marked CC0 can be downloaded, adapted, and shared.
limitation: Check the CC0 label and any third-party rights that apply to the intended use.

name: Unsplash
description: Find stock photography for presentations, editorial projects, and websites.
bestFor: Expressive stock photos for digital layouts and posts.
free: Photos under the Unsplash License allow commercial use without mandatory attribution.
limitation: Unsplash+ has separate terms. The free license restricts selling unmodified photos and competing collections.

name: Pexels
description: Download stock photos and video clips under the Pexels License.
bestFor: Quick stock footage and photography for creative projects.
free: Pexels photos and videos can be used without mandatory attribution.
limitation: The license restricts unchanged resale, misleading endorsement, and some uses of identifiable people.

name: Pixabay
description: Search stock images, video, and audio under the Pixabay Content License.
bestFor: Media for presentations and edited creative work.
free: Covered media can be used for free without mandatory credit.
limitation: Standalone redistribution and some brand-related uses are restricted. Check rights for the individual asset.

name: unDraw
description: Download customizable SVG illustrations for websites and presentations.
bestFor: Adding consistent illustrations to a product, portfolio, or slide deck.
free: Free personal and commercial use without attribution for covered illustrations.
limitation: The license restricts repackaging, competing catalogs, integrations, and AI training.

name: GitHub Student Developer Pack
description: Apply for GitHub Education and browse software, learning, and infrastructure partner offers.
bestFor: Students building and deploying software projects.
free: Accepted students can claim the available GitHub and partner benefits.
limitation: Student verification is required. Individual offers have separate eligibility, limits, and duration.

name: JetBrains Education
description: Apply for educational access to JetBrains development environments.
bestFor: Eligible students learning to code in tools such as IntelliJ IDEA and PyCharm.
free: The Student Pack includes free student IDE licenses.
limitation: Verification is required. The educational licenses are limited to non-commercial learning and research.

name: Autodesk Education
description: Get educational access to Autodesk software for learning CAD, 3D modeling, and engineering.
bestFor: Eligible students or educators working on class and learning projects.
free: Approved users receive renewable, one-year educational access to available software.
limitation: Autodesk verifies eligibility. Education access is for educational purposes.

name: Figma Education
description: Apply for free education access to Figma design and collaboration tools.
bestFor: Eligible students and educators doing design coursework.
free: Verified users get free access through Figma for Education.
limitation: The application route and eligibility differ between higher education and K–12.

name: Microsoft Education
description: Explore Microsoft 365 education options for browser-based documents, spreadsheets, and presentations.
bestFor: Students looking for Word, Excel, and PowerPoint for coursework.
free: Microsoft lists free browser access to Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.
limitation: Desktop applications and institution-managed features depend on the school or plan.

name: National Scholarship Portal
description: Find and apply for supported Indian scholarships through the official National Scholarship Portal.
bestFor: Students in India checking public scholarship schemes and application requirements.
free: The portal provides access to scholarship applications and scheme information.
limitation: Criteria, deadlines, documents, and award amounts depend on the scheme. Applications require registration.

name: SWAYAM
description: Study online courses from Indian universities and education bodies.
bestFor: Learners who want Indian course materials across school and higher education subjects.
free: Course materials and learning are available free of charge.
limitation: A SWAYAM certificate usually requires a paid, in-person proctored exam and course-specific eligibility.

name: National Career Service
description: Use India’s public employment portal to look for jobs, events, and career services.
bestFor: Job seekers exploring openings and career support in India.
free: The portal says it charges no fee for registration, applications, or interview processing.
limitation: An account is needed for application features. Individual roles have their own requirements.

name: Reactive Resume
description: Build a résumé in the browser and export it for a job application.
bestFor: Creating and maintaining a résumé with a dedicated web editor.
free: Use free templates and export to PDF or Word.
limitation: Create an account on the hosted service or set up your own instance.

name: Europass
description: Create a Europass CV for work or study applications in Europe.
bestFor: Applicants who want a multilingual European Commission CV format.
free: Use the free Europass CV and cover letter tools.
limitation: The templates follow Europass conventions. Check any format requested by the organization.

name: RenderCV
description: Turn a structured YAML file into a styled résumé or academic CV.
bestFor: People who want version control and repeatable PDF builds for their CV.
free: The free command-line tool supports template-based PDF rendering.
limitation: The local tool requires Python and configuration in YAML.

name: Canva Résumé Templates
description: Customize a résumé template in Canva’s browser editor.
bestFor: Creating a designed résumé quickly using a visual editor.
free: Free templates can be customized and downloaded in formats including PDF.
limitation: Choose a free template and check any Pro assets before exporting.

name: Harvard College Résumé and Cover Letter Guide
description: Use Harvard’s career guide to structure your résumé and write experience bullets.
bestFor: Writing or revising an early-career résumé and cover letter.
free: The public guide provides guidance and examples.
limitation: Examples are oriented toward Harvard College students. Adapt them to your experience and market.

name: Jekyll Résumé Template
description: Publish a text-first résumé website with a Jekyll template for GitHub Pages.
bestFor: Creating a simple public online résumé from a Git repository.
free: The template source is freely available under the MIT license.
limitation: Requires editing repository content and configuring GitHub Pages.

name: Squoosh
description: Compress or convert images locally in your browser with a side-by-side preview.
bestFor: Reducing image file size before publishing a site or sharing a file.
free: Use the free browser editor to compare codecs and quality settings.
limitation: Images stay on your device. The app collects some usage data, including before-and-after image sizes.

name: WebAIM WAVE
description: Check an individual webpage for common accessibility issues and review the results visually.
bestFor: A first accessibility review of a public page or a local page using the browser extension.
free: The public URL checker and browser extensions are available free.
limitation: Automated feedback still needs human evaluation. API access and bulk tooling are separate.

name: Colour Contrast Analyser
description: Sample colors on screen and test text or visual contrast in a desktop app.
bestFor: Checking contrast in mockups, documents, and interfaces.
free: Vispero provides a free desktop contrast checker with an eyedropper.
limitation: Contrast testing covers one part of an accessibility review.

name: WebAIM Contrast Checker
description: Enter text and background colors to calculate contrast and see WCAG pass criteria.
bestFor: Checking a design token or color pair without installing anything.
free: The web tool calculates contrast from your foreground and background colors.
limitation: Gradients, transparency, and complex backgrounds may require multiple checks.

name: NVDA
description: Read applications and websites aloud or with braille using a Windows screen reader.
bestFor: Accessing Windows applications without relying on visual output.
free: NVDA is available free from NV Access.
limitation: The screen reader is for Windows. Supported features depend on the application and assistive devices.

name: Subtitle Edit
description: Create, synchronize, and convert subtitle files for video.
bestFor: Editing caption timestamps and preparing subtitle files for publication.
free: The open-source project includes a subtitle editor and conversion tools.
limitation: Check supported formats and platform setup in the project’s release notes.

name: Audacity
description: Record, trim, and mix audio on your computer.
bestFor: Editing voice recordings, podcasts, or simple multi-track projects.
free: The editor and recorder are free and open source.
limitation: Some import and export formats require extra components.

name: GIMP
description: Retouch photos, work with layers, and create graphics in a desktop editor.
bestFor: Offline raster image editing with detailed controls.
free: The full desktop image editor is free and open source.
limitation: The editing workflow differs from browser-first design apps. Complex imported files may need adjustments.

name: HandBrake
description: Convert video files and adjust resolution or quality with desktop encoding presets.
bestFor: Making a smaller sharing copy or converting video to a common format.
free: The video transcoder is free and available for major desktop systems.
limitation: Encoding time depends on settings and hardware. Check output quality before replacing originals.

name: Project Gutenberg
description: Read and download digitized books, with a strong collection of older works.
bestFor: Finding a classic text to read or keep offline.
free: Most ebooks are free of charge and in the public domain in the United States.
limitation: Check item rights and your local copyright rules before redistribution outside the United States.

name: Standard Ebooks
description: Download carefully formatted editions of classic public-domain books.
bestFor: Reading classics on an e-reader with modern typography and navigation.
free: Download free editions in e-reader formats. Standard Ebooks dedicates its own work to the public domain.
limitation: Selection focuses on the U.S. public domain. Rights in other countries may differ.

name: OpenStax
description: Read peer-reviewed textbooks for common high-school and college subjects.
bestFor: Following a course without buying a textbook.
free: Every OpenStax textbook is free online, with free PDF options.
limitation: Physical copies cost money. Check the specific title for course coverage and license.

name: Zotero
description: Collect papers and webpages, annotate PDFs, and generate citations from a desktop library.
bestFor: Managing references for essays, research, and long writing projects.
free: Use the desktop reference manager for free. Online attachment storage starts at 300 MB.
limitation: An account is needed for syncing. Larger attachment storage plans are paid.

name: Kiwix
description: Download snapshots of Wikipedia and other learning materials to browse offline.
bestFor: Accessing reference materials with limited or unreliable internet.
free: The project offers free knowledge archives and reader software.
limitation: Download archives before going offline. Large archives require enough local space and snapshots can become outdated.

name: Language Transfer
description: Follow guided audio lessons that teach language patterns through examples.
bestFor: Starting a language through listening and active recall.
free: Stream or download the available free audio courses.
limitation: Course depth varies by language. Add reading and conversation practice separately.

name: OpenStreetMap
description: Browse and reuse a global map built by contributors.
bestFor: Finding open map data for a project or exploring local geography.
free: OpenStreetMap data is available under the Open Database License.
limitation: Attribute OpenStreetMap and check share-alike requirements. Hosted tiles have separate usage rules.

name: Anki
description: Create flashcards that reschedule reviews based on what you remember.
bestFor: Long-term review of vocabulary, concepts, and facts.
free: The desktop version is free. AnkiDroid is a free Android client.
limitation: The official AnkiMobile app for iOS is paid. Creating or choosing useful decks still takes work.

name: Bootstrap
description: Build responsive pages with a grid, standard interface components, and utilities.
bestFor: Prototyping sites and building interfaces with conventional HTML and CSS.
free: The library code is available under the MIT license.
limitation: Customize the styles and verify accessibility for your own components and content.

name: W3C Web Accessibility Introduction
description: Understand how accessible design helps people use websites and web applications.
bestFor: Designers and developers learning the basics of accessible interfaces.
free: Read the public W3C introduction and follow links to related guidance.
limitation: The overview introduces concepts. Detailed testing and implementation use separate guidance.

name: Libby
description: Borrow digital books, audiobooks, and magazines from participating libraries.
bestFor: Readers who already have or can obtain a compatible library card.
free: Install the app and borrow available titles for free through your library.
limitation: You need a valid card at a participating library. The collection and borrowing limits depend on the library.

name: Simon Tatham’s Portable Puzzle Collection
description: Play a library of single-player logic puzzles, including Mines, Net, Bridges, and Sudoku-style games.
bestFor: A quick solo puzzle with adjustable settings and fresh boards.
free: Open any puzzle’s browser version from the game list. Source code and desktop builds are available.
limitation: The puzzle interfaces and controls vary. Open a game’s instructions if you are new to it.

name: 0h h1
description: Fill a grid with two colors by working out which placements satisfy its rules.
bestFor: A short, untimed logic puzzle with small and larger grids.
free: Play generated boards in the browser without creating an account.
limitation: The game uses a two-color grid. Check the in-game options if you prefer a different appearance.

name: 2048 Classic
description: Slide matching tiles together and work up to 2048 in Gabriele Cirulli’s original number puzzle.
bestFor: A quick replayable number puzzle with simple controls.
free: Play the original game for free with arrow keys or touch swipes.
limitation: Each move shifts the whole board. Filling the grid without a possible move ends the run.

name: Waffle
description: Swap letters on a waffle-shaped grid to complete six intersecting words.
bestFor: A short daily English word puzzle.
free: Play the daily browser puzzle without creating an account.
limitation: Some archive or extra modes use ads or membership features. The current puzzle has a move limit.

name: Travle
description: Name the countries and connections needed to travel from one starting point to another.
bestFor: Working out a route across a map with several possible paths.
free: Play the daily geography challenge in a browser. Practice is available separately.
limitation: The game models some travel connections beyond simple land borders. Yesterday’s daily puzzle may be unavailable.

name: Globle
description: Guess a mystery country using warmer and colder hints displayed on a globe.
bestFor: Learning the relative positions of countries through repeated guesses.
free: Play the core country guessing puzzle in your browser.
limitation: The globe relies on visual color clues. Geographic edge cases follow the game’s own rules.

name: Worldle
description: Identify a country or territory from its outline and use distance and direction hints.
bestFor: A daily silhouette puzzle for learning country shapes.
free: The current daily puzzle is free to play in the browser.
limitation: The site shows ads. Archive access and saved cross-device statistics require Premium.

name: City Guesser
description: Watch real street footage and guess the city from what people, signs, and surroundings reveal.
bestFor: Getting better at identifying places from everyday visual clues.
free: Select a region or difficulty and start a browser round.
limitation: The rounds rely on visual clues and streamed video.

name: Seterra
description: Practice identifying countries, territories, capitals, and other places on a map.
bestFor: Learning locations systematically with topic-by-topic quizzes.
free: Seterra advertises hundreds of free geography quizzes.
limitation: Some quizzes focus on a single region or topic. GeoGuessr’s separate products have different access terms.

name: TimeGuessr
description: Estimate when and where a photograph was taken using visual and historical clues.
bestFor: Combining history knowledge with map and photo interpretation.
free: The browser site offers a daily challenge and free multiplayer games.
limitation: The rounds depend on visual cues. An account may be needed for some community features.

name: A Dark Room
description: Start with a fire in a dark room and uncover a story through small choices, exploration, and resource management.
bestFor: A minimalist text-based adventure that reveals its systems gradually.
free: The studio offers the original browser game for free and publishes its source code.
limitation: The game deliberately explains little up front. A full playthrough takes longer than a short puzzle.

name: Celeste Classic
description: Climb a pixel-art mountain in the original PICO-8 platformer by Maddy Thorson and Noel Berry.
bestFor: Practicing precise jumps and dash timing in short stages.
free: Play the developers’ original Classic game in the embedded browser player.
limitation: The difficulty rises quickly. The full Celeste release is a separate game.

name: Tetris
description: Stack falling shapes into complete lines in the official browser version of Tetris.
bestFor: A quick arcade puzzle that rewards planning ahead.
free: The official site hosts a free browser game.
limitation: The playfield gets faster over time. Check the game’s controls and pause menu before starting.

name: PAC-MAN Google Doodle
description: Guide PAC-MAN through a Google-shaped maze and collect dots while avoiding ghosts.
bestFor: Playing a short anniversary edition of the classic arcade maze game.
free: Launch the interactive anniversary Doodle directly on Google’s archive.
limitation: The archive hosts the Doodle’s custom maze. The game may play sound when started.

name: Doodle Champion Island Games
description: Explore an island as Lucky the cat, take on sports mini-games, and solve side quests.
bestFor: A longer retro-style browser game with several activities in one world.
free: The playable Google Doodle includes seven sports and optional side quests.
limitation: Some events need quick timing. The archive preserves the original event theme and team references.

name: Universal Paperclips
description: Turn a paperclip button into a growing production system in a minimalist incremental game.
bestFor: Exploring how simple upgrades turn into a longer strategy game.
free: Play the complete original game using its public web interface.
limitation: The developer designed the web interface for computers. The mobile apps are separate.

name: Cookie Clicker
description: Bake cookies, purchase upgrades, and build a production system in Orteil’s browser game.
bestFor: A low-pressure incremental game that can be played in short visits.
free: Play the original web edition at the developer’s site.
limitation: The browser page contains sponsored links. Paid editions for other platforms have separate terms.

name: Infinite Craft
description: Drag two elements together and see what new item they create.
bestFor: Open-ended experimentation with combinations and surprising results.
free: The core game is available on Neal Agarwal’s site with four starting elements.
limitation: Discoveries and some other features send gameplay data to the site’s servers.

name: Little Alchemy 2
description: Combine basic elements and build up a catalog of materials, objects, and inventions.
bestFor: A relaxed discovery game for trying combinations at your own pace.
free: The official browser game offers a large set of free items to discover.
limitation: The browser version and mobile versions have separate features. The official hints site can spoil recipes.

name: Flexbox Froggy
description: Write CSS to put frogs on their lilypads while learning flexbox alignment and layout.
bestFor: Practicing CSS flexbox in small interactive lessons.
free: The full browser game is free, with selectable languages and level instructions.
limitation: The lessons focus on flexbox. CSS Grid and other topics have separate games.

name: NASA Explore Mars
description: Drive a rover, collect information about Martian rocks, and send it back to Earth.
bestFor: Introducing children to rover navigation and planetary science.
free: NASA Space Place provides the game directly with instructions and mission context.
limitation: The game uses a simplified model of rover operation. Audio guidance is available alongside visual elements.

name: Codenames Online
description: Give one-word clues to connect the right words in a team deduction game.
bestFor: Remote game night with friends who enjoy word associations.
free: Czech Games Edition offers the browser game for free. Create a room and share it with friends.
limitation: Plan how the group will talk. The publisher describes using a separate voice or video call.

name: Gartic Phone
description: Pass sentences and drawings around a group to see how the original idea changes.
bestFor: A casual game night for friends who like drawing and writing prompts.
free: Start a browser session with a nickname, then invite friends to your room.
limitation: The sessions rely on player-submitted drawings and text. The developer suggests a separate voice call.

name: skribbl.io
description: Take turns drawing a secret word while other players race to guess it.
bestFor: A fast drawing game with friends or an open lobby.
free: The browser game is free, with both public play and private rooms.
limitation: Public lobbies include chat and content from strangers. Choose a private room for a known group.

name: Board Game Arena
description: Join live or turn-based online tables for a collection of licensed board games.
bestFor: Playing tabletop games remotely at a pace that suits your group.
free: A free account can play many games and join a Premium table started by another player.
limitation: An account is required. Starting a table for some games and certain other features require Premium.

name: Lichess
description: Play chess, challenge a friend or a computer, and work through tactics puzzles in your browser.
bestFor: Playing or studying chess with free puzzles, boards, and analysis.
free: Lichess offers free games, puzzles, lessons, and analysis without advertising or paid tiers.
limitation: Use an account for ratings, tracked progress, and tournaments.

name: PDF24 Creator
description: Compress, convert, merge, or print to PDF on your PC with the offline PDF24 desktop app.
bestFor: Handling sensitive documents locally on Windows.
free: The offline toolkit and PDF printer are free for private and business use.
limitation: The desktop app requires Windows and a local installation. PDF24’s online tools are a separate option.

name: W3C Easy Checks
description: Follow a practical checklist to spot common issues with headings, keyboard access, contrast, and media.
bestFor: A first manual accessibility review of a website.
free: The W3C guide provides public step-by-step checks with examples and instructions.
limitation: These basic checks cover only part of a full accessibility evaluation.

name: ANDI
description: Inspect accessible names and descriptions and flag common web issues with a browser bookmarklet.
bestFor: Understanding what assistive technology may announce for interactive controls.
free: The U.S. Social Security Administration provides the bookmarklet and documentation for free.
limitation: Your browser must allow bookmarklets. Use its findings as one part of a manual review.

name: LosslessCut
description: Extract sections from video and audio without re-encoding supported formats.
bestFor: Quickly trimming large recordings while preserving original quality.
free: Free releases of the open-source desktop app are available from the project’s repository.
limitation: Lossless cuts can depend on codec keyframe positions. Some app stores charge for their builds.
